revision_of_prior_candidate: A custom task-capable call_tool is not the smallest safe seam. The released macro/router surface permits keeping the SDK-generated router-first call_tool and moving task materialization into the registered tool handler after router policy and extractor validation.
exact_source_evidence: #[tool_handler] generates call_tool only when the ServerHandler impl does not define one. The generated method constructs ToolCallContext and calls the selected ToolRouter.call.

The same macro preserves user-defined get_info and other ServerHandler methods, so an impl can advertise Tasks and override get_task/update_task/cancel_task while still letting the macro generate router-first call_tool.

ToolRouter.call rejects disabled routes before invoking a handler and converts standard Parameters deserialization failures into a tool error result. Thus a registered task-capable tool receives control only after current route availability and typed argument extraction have succeeded.

ToolCallContext/handler extractors expose RequestContext, Parameters

, RequestState, InputResponses and Extensions. An authenticated principal inserted by application middleware can be retrieved as Extension; RequestStateCodec associated_data can bind that principal plus tool/method/argument digest.

IntoCallToolResult supports InputRequiredResult and CallToolResponse, and CallToolResponse includes Task(CreateTaskResult). Therefore a registered tool handler can return side-effect-free InputRequired on round one and a CreateTaskResult on round two without replacing call_tool.

InputRequiredResult explicitly permits requestState with no inputRequests. RequestStateCodec provides HMAC-SHA256 integrity, associated-data binding and TTL; single-use still requires server-side state.

ServerHandler get_task/update_task/cancel_task are overrideable. Stock TaskManager itself has no storage backend trait: TaskContext privately contains Arc<Mutex<TaskManagerInner>>, and TaskManager.spawn always creates a fresh UUIDv4 in its process-local HashMap.

The generic Service dispatcher checks the client's Tasks capability after call_tool returns a Task. A task-capable registered handler must therefore check client Tasks capability inside the handler before persistent create-or-get; the dispatcher check is only a wire guard, not a materialization fence.
smallest_candidate_shape: Use #[tool_router] on the server's registered tools and #[tool_handler] on ServerHandler, but do NOT implement call_tool. Let the macro-generated router-first call_tool remain authoritative for route disablement and extractor/argument validation.
Implement get_info manually with enable_tools().enable_tasks(), and implement get_task/update_task/cancel_task against the custom persistent store.

For each task-capable registered tool, accept typed Parameters<Args>, RequestContext<RoleServer>, RequestState, and an application Extension<Principal> (or equivalent authenticated principal extractor).

Round 1: after router/extractor validation and before any task/effect, verify client Tasks capability. Mint server op_id, seal {op_id, protocol version/expiry as needed} with RequestStateCodec associated_data over principal + tools/call + tool name + canonical args digest, return InputRequiredResult::from_request_state.

Round 2: router/extractors run again, so policy revocation/disabled route and argument validity are current. Open requestState with the re-derived associated data; then atomically persistent create-or-get(op_id, intent_hash). Return CreateTaskResult::new(seed_task) for both the winner and exact duplicate retry.

Only the create winner may claim/schedule execution. The persistent executor/redriver must use a monotonic attempt generation and invoke the factored business effect, not recursively call the tool handler. Terminal state writes are generation-CAS; external effects still require effect-side idempotency or fencing.
tasks/get/update/cancel operate on the persistent task row; any in-task MRTR/input request persistence is a separate custom responsibility because stock TaskContext is tied to TaskManagerInner.
why_router_first_matters: The official TaskDemo manually parses arguments and branches to TaskManager.spawn before ToolRouter for task-capable slow_sum. That example therefore has to duplicate policy/validation. Keeping macro-generated call_tool and returning Task from the registered tool handler avoids this duplication: disabled-route checks and standard extractors run before application task materialization on every MRTR round.

strict_phase1_boundary: The seam removes a policy/validation duplication problem but does not remove the resident durable store/executor/redriver dependency. It therefore does not satisfy strict Phase-1 by itself. Handle recovery, execution liveness, and external-effect duplicate safety remain separate proof obligations.
